papers.title: Identification and isolation of migratory subpopulations of cancer cells using microfluidics with fluid walls
papers.abstract: Microfluidic assays have great potential for investigating cancer cell migration, a key process underlying metastasis which remains a major clinical challenge. However, adoption by biologists is limited due to complex fabrication and operation methods combined with difficulty in retrieving cells of interest. We jet-print dumbbell-shaped microfluidic environments with fluid walls in standard Petri dishes in seconds using standard growth media and immiscible oil. Prostate cancer cells and chemoattractant (bovine serum) are introduced into each end using local transient differences in Laplace pressure to enable spatial confinement. Automated live-cell imaging monitors chemotaxis towards serum using standard microscopes, as the confining fluid walls are optically transparent. Distinct subpopulations of migratory cells exhibit different morphologies and motilities, assessed using a custom machine-learning segmentation model. Then, we leverage the reconfigurability of fluid walls to isolate and retrieve rapidly-migrating single cells. This demonstrates that fluid-walled microfluidics is a versatile and accessible approach for investigating cancer cell migration at single-cell resolution, offering new opportunities to examine cellular heterogeneity in metastasis.

papers.title: Ferrybots: Programmable Hydrogel Microbots for Rapid Magnetic Navigation and Modular Function
papers.abstract: Untethered microrobots could enable localized delivery, sensing, and intervention in confined biological and engineered environments. Magnetic actuation is especially attractive for such systems because it provides remote, fuel-free control, but practical magnetic microrobots remain difficult to manufacture and functionalize. High magnetic loading can interfere with polymerization and structural integrity, while integrating application-specific payloads directly into the robot body often requires the entire material formulation to be redesigned. Here, we introduce Ferrybots, programmable hydrogel microrobots that physically separate magnetic navigation from functional cargo. An automated droplet-on-demand microfluidic flow-lithography process confines high-concentration ferrofluid cores within photopolymerized poly (ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) structures, enabling magnetic loading to be programmed through core number and spacing without uniformly dispersing magnetic particles throughout the hydrogel. The process achieved a minimum fabrication cycle time of 15 s. Ferrybots exhibited magnetic-dose-dependent translation and rotation, branched-channel steering, out-of-plane obstacle traversal, and rapid translation, with two-core robots following an external magnet at speeds up to the 9000 mm/min limit of the actuation system. Differences in magnetic loading also enabled sequential selective navigation of distinct Ferrybot populations. Using PEGDA 575 as a common interface material, independently formulated hydrogel cargo modules could subsequently be fused to preformed Ferrybots while preserving navigation. Separately, cargo modules enabled composition-dependent molecular release and oxygen-responsive sensing through 1-mm-thick skin-mimicking optical phantoms representing a broad range of skin types. By decoupling locomotion from function, Ferrybots provide a common magnetic vehicle that can be combined with interchangeable delivery, sensing, or responsive-material modules, offering a general strategy for rapidly adapting microrobots to different applications.

papers.title: Circular-Arc Modal Migration for Ultrasound Imaging--Part I: Finite-Arc Spectral Theory and Stolt-Pullback Factorization
papers.abstract: Circular-arc ultrasound imaging requires a spectral construction that accommodates radius-dependent propagation and the spatially varying phase of offset-source transmission. This first of two articles develops Circular-Arc Modal Migration (CAMM), a direct Stolt-type imaging framework in angular modal coordinates. Starting from a first-Born acoustic model, angular decomposition and local radial Stolt mappings convert channel spectra into fields for coherent image synthesis. The offset transmit phase is represented by a phase-screen factorization through reusable spectral factors and spatially weighted fields. A scalar-pullback approximation simplifies this correction to reading one reference image at a geometrically fitted radial coordinate. Both realizations share the same modal construction. Error controls address local radial synthesis, transmit-path expansion, scalar approximation, and phase-screen truncation, with direct integration verifying the separated numerical evaluation. Same-RF point-target comparisons show that scalar pullback closely preserves the principal peak positions and widths of phase-screen imaging in the compact semicircular configuration, while phase screens better control surrounding responses in the shallow convex examples. The retained modal spectrum, frequency band, image radius, and source displacement guide this accuracy--computation choice. CAMM thereby extends direct spectral image formation to circular arcs and supplies the theoretical and numerical basis for the image-quality and performance studies in Part~II.

papers.title: Machine learning assisted multi-level differentiation of blood cells using multi-frequency electro-mechanical impedance cytometry
papers.abstract: We report a multi-frequency microfluidic impedance cytometer with multimodal measurement of electrical and mechanical cell properties. Using the large feature set from the multimodality, we implemented machine learning assisted differentiation of cells. We have demonstrated a constriction-equipped channel to study the mechanical cell properties, and integrated multiple microelectrodes that capture electric field information pertaining to various stages of cell transit. Our system works over a wide frequency range from 800 kHz to 8 MHz. We developed a machine learning workflow to classify cells using our multi-modal data. Using this platform to show blood cell differentiation, our system shows minimum F1 score to be 0.92, minimizing both false negatives and false positives, which is important for medical diagnosis. Furthermore, we also identified the presence of two populations in the mixed sample of neutrophils and PBMCs. Our workflow allows classification of cells in a new sample along with identification of top 5 distinguishing parameters out of 70+ features extracted from the raw impedance signal.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal multiplexing on subretinal prosthesis increases selectivity of the network-mediated stimulation
papers.abstract: Subretinal photovoltaic implants (PRIMA) provide form vision in patients blinded by age-related macular degeneration. The success of this approach is attributed in part to the network-mediated stimulation, which preserves many features of the natural retinal signal encoding. For efficient stimulation of bipolar cells (BC) with smaller pixels, electric field confinement should be relaxed, yet direct activation of the retinal ganglion cells (RGC) should be avoided. Here we present a new method for selective stimulation of bipolar cells using image multiplexing - sequential presentation of the image's components in several subframes. With sizes of the subframe islands optimized by computational modelling, the selectivity of network (BC) mediated retinal stimulation increased over 5 times in rats. Using this approach, electric field confinement can be relaxed, allowing pixels as small as 20 m to efficiently stimulate bipolar cells, while avoiding direct stimulation of RGCs and preserving high contrast of the pattern. This software-based improvement enables higher visual acuity of prosthetic vision without a change in implanted hardware.

papers.title: Effective utilization of xylose-rich substrates for butyric acid production by Clostridium tyrobutyricum ATCC 25755 despite carbon catabolite repression
papers.abstract: Carbon catabolite repression (CCR) can restrict xylose utilization during butyric acid production from lignocellulosic hydrolysates by Clostridium tyrobutyricum ATCC 25755. This study evaluated CCR behavior using 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2-DG), a glucose analog, and examined the effects of glucose-xylose composition on mixed-sugar fermentation. 2-DG caused concentration-dependent growth inhibition in xylose-containing medium, indicating CCR-like behavior. However, xylose was partially co-consumed in the presence of glucose or 2-DG, suggesting incomplete inhibition. In batch fermentations with 80 g/L total sugars, the overall xylose consumption rate declined from 2.68 to 0.53 g/L/h as the initial glucose concentration increased from 20 to 60 g/L. Nevertheless, a xylose-rich mixture (20 g/L glucose and 60 g/L xylose) achieved an overall total sugar consumption rate of 3.54 g/L/h and a butyric acid productivity of 1.22 g/L/h, comparable to those with 80 g/L glucose alone (3.64 and 1.26 g/L/h, respectively). Detectable xylose isomerase activity during glucose-xylose co-utilization further supported incomplete repression of xylose metabolism. In xylose-rich rice straw hydrolysate (5.0 g/L glucose and 15.1 g/L xylose), both sugars were completely consumed, producing 7.68 g/L butyric acid. These findings suggest that xylose-rich mixtures can support effective sugar utilization and butyric acid production by C. tyrobutyricum despite its CCR-like behavior.

papers.title: Volumetric building blocks: A simple and modular approach to create perfusable models via assembly of volumetrically printed subunits
papers.abstract: Tomographic volumetric additive manufacturing (tVAM) enables rapid 3D printing of constructs with intricate, freestanding geometries. Besides demonstrating very promising applications in tissue engineering and biofabrication, a limitation of the technology has been the relatively high material consumption and limited maximal model size due to optical and technical constraints. Here we demonstrate the fabrication and use of highly modular hollow structures created with tVAM to produce large scale tubular systems that allow the formation of complex, hollow networks beyond the build space of commercial tVAM devices. In many cases, it can reduce the overall dead volume used for printing by more than 50% compared to printing the whole structure at once. As proof of concept, we made a channel system recapitulating the physiological complexity of human vasculature in vitro. The system was tested with liquid flow dynamic and stent placement into stenosed segments to show that leaktight models could be created. Further, by using gelatin methacryloyl, a large-scale system out of seven single units could be created and effectively endothelialized, showing the potential of the approach for fabrication of physiological stent placement phantoms or vascular tissue models.

papers.title: Engineered endocrine objects tolerate hypoxia in macroencapsulation devices and enable subcutaneous engraftment in diabetic mice
papers.abstract: Islet encapsulation has been pursued for decades as a potential immunosuppression-free transplantation strategy to treat type 1 diabetes (T1D). The encapsulation device protects islets from immune cell-contact mediated killing, but it also prevents vascular penetration and intra-islet vascularization, leading to poor mass transfer and islet central necrosis. In healthy pancreas, islets with sizes > ~40 m are vascularized while non-islet endocrine cell clusters below ~40 m exist without internal capillaries. Here, we developed scalable and reproducible engineered endocrine objects (EEOs) as small as ~47 m by mesh-induced fragmentation of native islets, followed by a recovery culture. Under hypoxic culture condition (1% O2 for 24 hours), EEOs showed enhanced viability of >90%, compared to 49% for the native islet control. With a flat, thin (0.5-mm-thick) alginate-based macroencapsulation device, rat EEOs at a marginal dose of 300 islet equivalents (IEQ) achieved glycemic control for over 5 weeks in the challenging, hypoxic subcutaneous space of immunocompetent diabetic mice. The engrafted mice displayed near-physiological glycemic profiles upon glucose challenge, and the retrieved EEOs showed enhanced viability with significantly reduced central necrosis compared with native islets. Overall, engineering hypoxia-resistance into cellular products mitigates intrinsic constraints of encapsulation devices, offering a promising strategy for convenient, immunosuppression-free subcutaneous islet transplantation.

papers.title: Freebie: A Multi-Camera System for Real-Time Markerless Hand Tracking in Non-Human Primates
papers.abstract: Objective. Neural decoders for dexterous finger movements are limited by the accuracy with which ground truth movement is measured. In non-human primates (NHPs), hand kinematics are typically recorded with instrumentation that constrains movement dimensionality. We evaluated whether a markerless camera system could replace conventional methods for tracking movements in real time. Approach. We developed Freebie, a real-time markerless system for tracking NHP finger movements. Keypoints detected online were used in place of manipulandum bend sensor signals. Two NHPs performed tasks by flexing fingers to move a virtual hand into target zones. The virtual hand was directly controlled using bend sensors or Freebie-derived kinematics, or indirectly controlled through a Kalman filter (KF) decoding kinematics from forearm electromyographic (EMG) activity. We quantified Freebie's accuracy relative to manual labels, agreement with bend sensor measurements, and latencies. We assessed online performance under Freebie control and compared EMG KFs trained using Freebie-derived labels with those trained using bend-sensor-derived labels. Main Results. We observed a median end-to-end latency of 15.8 ms at a 30 FPS camera acquisition rate, and 16.2 ms at 60 FPS. Freebie labels closely tracked bend sensor positions (median |r|=0.96). Median keypoint errors were 1.7 to 6.5 pixels, below the 20-pixel width of the smallest tracked finger. Direct Freebie control did not differ from bend sensor control on five of six online metrics; path efficiency was higher with Freebie. EMG KFs trained on Freebie-derived labels performed similarly to those trained on bend sensor labels online. When evaluated offline, models trained with Freebie had lower error. Significance. These findings indicate that bend sensors are not required to obtain finger labels for training a decoder: markerless keypoints alone provided effective labels. This is an important first step towards real-time tracking of more complex movements, beyond what could be easily measured with a manipulandum.

papers.title: Lipid Anchor Chemistry and Spacer Architecture Influence DNA Availability and Light-Directed Cell Printing
papers.abstract: Precise control over cellular interactions is critical to understanding the complex underpinnings of disease. DNA-printing of cells (DPC), a technology that uses complementary DNA to program cellular interactions, has the potential to enable precision cell printing. However, the simplicity of printing is undermined by the stability of anchoring moieties. This manuscript systematically investigates how commercially available hydrophobic DNA anchor and co-anchor chemistries influence DNA availability and light-directed DPC (LD-DPC) printability. Using cholesterol, tocopherol, and cholesterol-tocopherol modifications with defined spacer architectures, we evaluated how anchor chemistry and molecular architecture influence functional DNA presentation at the cell surface. Notably, incorporating additional polyethylene glycol spacers between lipid anchors and DNA enhances functional DNA availability and patterning performance. While cholesterol-based anchors provide the highest initial surface loading, tocopherol-containing anchors promote greater spatial dispersion and cell-capture efficiency during printing. Notably, multiple anchor/co-anchor combinations maintain functional DNA presentation at room temperature and in serum-containing media. These findings demonstrate that lipid anchor identity and spacer architecture strongly influence the availability of membrane-associated DNA and the performance of light-directed DNA printing of cells. Collectively, these results provide practical guidance for designing stable nucleic-acid-modified cell interfaces using commercially available lipid-DNA chemistries.

papers.title: A network of syringe-injectable bioelectronics for closed-loop therapeutic rescue
papers.abstract: An on-body network of sensors and drug delivery implants could transform treatments for rapid-onset morbidities that require bystander intervention. During opioid overdoses, for example, lone and incapacitated victims often cannot self-administer life-saving naloxone in the minutes before respiratory collapse. However, the bulkiness of existing closed-loop systems threatens patient acceptance. Here, we present the Rapid Emergency Subcutaneous platform (RES-Q), a network of wearable sensors and syringe-implantable autoinjectors for closed-loop therapy. RES-Q implants are similar in size to FDA-approved drug rod implants and fit inside 6-gauge needles to facilitate outpatient administration. Informed by implant fibrosis fracture mechanics, RES-Q employs miniature jet injectors that deliver 0.4 mg human-relevant doses of naloxone through fibrotic encapsulation for rapid uptake. RES-Q implants communicate with wearable sensors through tissue conductivity, resulting in 25 nA standby current draws that ensure long-term functionality. In swine, we sequentially trigger multiple implants using ionic tissue communication. In rats, RES-Q detects fentanyl overdoses using wearable photoplethysmography sensors and performs autonomous, dose-titratable rescue in < 6 minutes.

papers.title: RNAtomy: A Structure-Aware RNA Foundation Model for Transferable Structural and Functional Representations
papers.abstract: RNA plays a critical and diverse role in gene expression, catalysis, regulation, and molecular recognition. This functional versatility arises from the interplay between nucleotide sequence, structural organization, and cellular context. Nevertheless, most RNA foundation models are pretrained primarily using sequence or secondary-structure information, while the systematic integration of three-dimensional geometric and conformational features remains comparatively underexplored. Here, we introduce RNAtomy, a self-supervised RNA foundation model designed to learn the structural anatomy of RNA from inter-nucleotide geometry and residue-level conformational descriptors. Its design has three main components: 1) joint masked reconstruction of pairwise geometry and residue-level descriptors to connect spatial organization with local conformation; 2) a hybrid Mamba-Transformer backbone in which Mamba blocks efficiently propagate global context, while shifted-window attention compensates for the absence of explicit content-dependent token interactions in Mamba by modeling relationships within local regions of the pairwise map; and 3) axis-aware feature-wise linear modulation that maps nucleotide-level conformations to the row and column axes of pairwise geometry. We assess RNAtomy across seven diverse tasks involving structural and functional predictions at the nucleotide, nucleotide-pair, and RNA levels. RNAtomy achieved particularly strong performance on structural tasks, outperforming established RNA foundation models and task-specific approaches in contact and long-range base-pair prediction. Its representations also transferred effectively to interaction-related tasks, despite the substantial differences between these applications and the structural pretraining objective. On functional tasks, RNAtomy achieved superior performance in translation-related prediction and regulatory-element identification. Notably, RNAtomy achieved these results despite being pretrained on a substantially smaller training set than the RNA foundation models used as baselines. Together, these results highlight how rich structural information, when learned through an expressive architecture, can support transferable RNA representations across biologically distinct structural and functional applications.

papers.title: Microfluidic Assembly of Synthetic Tissues from Synthetic Cells
papers.abstract: Biological tissues demonstrate emergent properties arising from the collective interactions of individual cells. While developmental biology has revealed the molecular mechanisms that control processes such as cell-cell adhesion, cellular rearrangements, and mechanosignalling, understanding how the local interactions lead to tissue scale mechanics remains challenging due to the biochemical complexity of living systems. Minimal synthetic tissue models allow us to isolate and examine the underlying physical principles. Liposomes as synthetic cells provide a biomimetic platform with tunable membrane characteristics and the ability to assemble into more complex structures. We present minimal tissue mimetic models based on synthetic cells that enable quantification to link microscale interactions to macroscale features in minimal synthetic tissues. To facilitate these studies, we have optimized the solvent mediated dewetting method to produce some of the highest throughput. This high yield enabled us to develop tissue mimetic structures in two complementary configurations: a freestanding monolayer and a confined microfluidic assembly. Morphological analysis in freestanding model revealed that adhesion-mediated packing induced significant deformation of synthetic cells, accompanied by changes in circularity and eccentricity. The fluorescent assay in confined model demonstrated that adhesive tissue formation reduced transport rates by decreasing pore size and increasing pathway tortuosity while maintaining mechanical stability under flow. Together, these minimal tissue-mimetic platforms provide a quantitative framework for linking synthetic-cell properties, collective organization, and emergent tissue-scale phenomena.

papers.title: Quantification of Local Mesostructural Deformation of the Myocardium using DENSE MRI and a Novel Set of Strain Attributes
papers.abstract: Measuring myocardial deformation is central to understanding the mechanical behavior of both the healthy and the diseased heart. While myocardial deformation is quantified via medical imaging in the form of strain, numerous definitions have been used in the engineering and clinical literature, resulting in inconsistencies in interpreting mechanistic changes in myocardial function. Additionally, current strain definitions lack the robustness required to relate quantitative changes in strain to changes in the myocardial mesostructure. Hence, the goal of this work was to propose a novel set of logarithmic, mesostructure-based strain attributes, by leveraging the upper triangular (QR) decomposition theorem. These strain attributes were then compared with the polar Green strain, the most widely used strain definition for the myocardium. Ten healthy subjects were scanned via displacement encoding with stimulated echoes (DENSE). From these images, a 3-dimensional (3D) displacement field was obtained, from which both 3D Green strains and strain attributes were calculated and compared. The results of this work revealed that the two strain definitions yield significantly different deformation profiles of the myocardium (p < 0.05), with strain attributes predicting relatively more spatial heterogeneity compared to the Green strains -- a finding consistent with similar studies that quantified mesostructural myocardial deformation. Additionally, the strain attributes revealed the myocardium to be compressible, challenging the common assumption of incompressibility. By capturing the deformation along the mesostructure, the strain attributes enable intuitive characterizations of cardiac disease, providing clinicians with deeper mechanistic insights into left ventricular function and serving as predictive markers of adverse remodeling.

papers.title: Tetracycline-Responsive Aptazymes Enable Tunable Expression of Self-Amplifying RNA
papers.abstract: Self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) enables prolonged protein expression at substantially lower doses than conventional mRNA. Beyond vaccination, uncontrolled saRNA replication raises safety concerns. Overexpressing the gene of interest exhausts cellular resources and leads to immunogenic double-stranded saRNA. Here, we investigated Tet-On and Tet-Off tetracycline-responsive aptazymes to control saRNA amplification exogenously. Insertion of the aptazymes within the 3' untranslated region (UTR) resulted in significantly less eGFP expression, while insertion in the subgenomic promoter region maintained expression. Additionally, we found that 33% N1-methyl-pseudouridine (m1{Psi}) substitution maintained eGFP expression, while complete substitution dramatically reduced it. At physiologically relevant tetracycline doses, Tet-On and Tet-Off aptazymes lowered eGFP expression 1.5-fold and 2.1-fold, respectively, relative to control saRNA. These in vitro results demonstrate saRNA with tunable expression.

papers.title: Human cortical mosaicoids reveal impact on spatial organization and progressive loss of cross-genotype functional coupling in MECP2 mosaicism
papers.abstract: Cellular mosaicism arising from postzygotic mutation or X-chromosome inactivation is a major determinant of phenotypic variability in neurodevelopmental disorders. Rett syndrome, which is caused by mutations in the X-linked gene MECP2, is a striking example in which wild-type and mutant neural cells coexist within the developing brain. However, how MECP2 mosaicism shapes human cortical tissue organization and circuit assembly remains poorly understood. Here, we developed MosaicoidX, a human mosaic organoid platform combining controlled co-seeding of isogenic wild-type and MECP2-mutant hiPS cells with genotype-resolved calcium imaging, computational modeling, and single-cell transcriptomics. FACS-based single-cell seeding enabled reproducible generation of cortical mosaicoids with defined initial genotype ratios. Structural two-photon imaging revealed mutation-dependent spatial organization, with MECP2[V247X] mosaicoids (harboring a truncating mutation) showing pronounced skewing of radial and angular segregation compared with MECP2[R306C] mosaicoids (harboring a missense mutation). MosaicoidSim, a computational model, showed that genotype-dependent adhesion, proliferation, differentiation, and migration parameters can account for the emergence of mosaic spatial patterning. Genotype-resolved two-photon calcium imaging demonstrated asymmetric functional connectivity, in which wild-type neuron pairs formed stronger and more frequent activity-coupled interactions than mutant-mutant or wild-type-mutant pairs. Finally, single-cell RNA-seq combined with ligand-receptor analysis inferred genotype- and cell-type-dependent alterations in synaptic signaling pathways, including GABAergic and neurexin-neuroligin interactions. Together, these results show that MECP2 mosaicism actively shapes organoid development through both cell-autonomous and non-cell-autonomous mechanisms. MosaicoidX provides a general framework for dissecting genetic mosaicism in Rett syndrome and other mosaic neurodevelopmental disorders.

papers.title: Synchrotron diffraction reveals distinct collagen-associated distributions of EGFR-targeted antibody and affibody in pancreatic tumors
papers.abstract: Significance: Tumor extracellular matrix may influence the distribution of targeted agents differently across molecular formats. We compared how an antibody and an affibody targeting the same receptor distribute relative to collagen associated tissue structure in pancreatic tumors. Methods: Cetuximab IRDye700DX, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) targeted fluorescent antibody, and ABY029, an EGFR targeted fluorescent affibody, were coadministered intravenously to 12 athymic nude mice bearing orthotopic pancreatic tumors: eight AsPC1 and four PANC1. Tumors were harvested at 3 or 24 h after injection, with four AsPC1 and two PANC1 mice at each time. Fluorescence images from 21 tissue slices were registered to scanning synchrotron X ray diffraction (XRD) maps to compare the distribution of each agent with local collagen associated diffraction intensity. Results: Cetuximab XRD correlations were negative in all 12 mice at every evaluated binning scale (100 to 400 microns, all adjusted P = 0.0039). Cohort average correlations were more negative for cetuximab than ABY029 at all four scales (paired adjusted P = 0.0137 to 0.0381). Conclusions: Cetuximab exhibited consistent inverse spatial associations with collagen-associated diffraction and stronger cohort-average associations than ABY029. These findings show that agents targeting the same receptor can differ in their relationships with local tissue structure and support spatially resolved assessment of tissue access when selecting molecular formats for imaging and therapy.

papers.title: Directing Cell Fate via Spatiotemporally Patterned Viscoelasticity Driven by Dynamic Crosslink Exchange
papers.abstract: The spatially and temporally varied mechanical and biochemical properties of the extracellular matrix (ECM) are critical regulators of cell function. Despite the emerging importance of ECM viscoelasticity in dictating cell fate, suitable biomaterials systems enabling spatiotemporal control over matrix viscoelasticity to direct cell function in physiologically relevant 3D contexts are lacking. A dynamic covalent hydrogel platform was developed that enables user-defined, in situ modulation of stress relaxation kinetics decoupled from bulk network stiffness via self-contained, radical-free photochemistries. By introducing photocaged alkoxyamines into initially rapidly relaxing hydrazone-based networks, the viscoelasticity of the networks can be tuned on demand by converting the hydrazone crosslinks to more stable oxime crosslinks following light exposure. This hydrazone-to-oxime bond exchange drives a dramatic shift in stress relaxation half time from approximately ~10^2 s to ~10^4 s within a single, continuous matrix, without altering stiffness or introducing cytotoxicity. This platform enabled real-time control over cellular adaptations to spatiotemporally patterned viscoelastic mechanical cues, directing fibroblast morphological transitions in 2D, human neural progenitor cell stemness maintenance in 3D, and neurite outgrowth from encapsulated motor neuron spheroids. This phototunable hydrogel system represents a robust platform for selectively patterning viscoelastic cues to direct mechanosensitive cell fate transitions.

papers.title: Engineering the thumb loop of T7 RNA polymerase improves the integrity of long RNA transcripts
papers.abstract: Incomplete transcripts complicate therapeutic mRNA manufacturing, particularly for long constructs such as self-amplifying RNA (saRNA). Their mechanisms remain poorly understood, hindering targeted improvements to mRNA integrity, a critical quality attribute. Here, our goal was to engineer the thumb loop of T7 RNA polymerase (RNAP) to improve transcript integrity. Using templates derived from a common 12 kb RNA sequence, we observed decreasing integrity as transcript length increased. Substitution of proline residues within the thumb loop improved integrity across 4, 8, and 12 kb transcripts, with several variants outperforming the previously reported K389A variant on the 12 kb template. Further substitutions identified M362K as the top performer and K363R as beneficial, implicating local conformation and electrostatic interactions. M362K retained its integrity-enhancing effect with N1-methylpseudouridine or 5-methylcytidine incorporated during transcription. These findings identify the thumb loop as a target for improving the integrity of long, chemically modified RNA transcripts.

papers.title: Bioinspired living nerve conduit with coupled physiological signals enables functional recovery of peripheral nerve
papers.abstract: Long-distance peripheral nerve injury causes severe tissue dysfunction. However, current repair strategies fail to recapitulate the native regenerative microenvironment with coupled physiological signals, hindering functional restoration. Here, we report a bioinspired living neural conduit (LNC) featuring a tri-layered, nerve-like architecture comprising a hydrogel bilayer, nano-grooved ferroelectric polymer stripes, and living Schwann cells, imparting coupled biomechanical, bioelectrical, and biochemical signals. The LNC achieves exceptional adaptability at the injured nerve interface, enabling nerve tissue-matched electrical conductivity, conformal and sutureless integration, and sustained secretion of pro-regenerative exosomes and growth factors (2.2-fold neurotrophic and 1.4-fold angiogenic factor upregulation). In rodent long-gap nerve defect models, the LNC orchestrates intraneural angiogenesis, accelerates axonal outgrowth, and enhances remyelination, achieving unprecedented motor function recovery without neuroma formation or adverse immune responses. By faithfully recapitulating the coupled biophysical and biochemical microenvironment of native nerve repair, the LNC offers a promising strategy towards functional restoration in challenging tissue injuries.

papers.title: Programming Primary Schwann Cells with Circular RNA Delivered by Listeria Drones
papers.abstract: Efficient transient genetic engineering of primary cells remains a major challenge in regenerative medicine, immunotherapy, and other cell-based therapies, as many therapeutically relevant cell types are refractory to conventional gene delivery. Primary Schwann cells (SCs) hold particular promise for peripheral nerve and spinal cord regeneration, yet nonviral gene delivery into these cells remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate transient programming of primary rat SCs using circular RNA (circRNA) delivered by attenuated, self-destructing Listeria monocytogenes (Lm) drones. These engineered bacteria invade mammalian cells, escape the phagosome, synthesize and circularize target RNA under inducible control, and undergo programmed lysis to release circRNA into the host cytosol for IRES-mediated protein synthesis. Previously validated in cancer and immune cell lines, this platform had not been evaluated in primary cells. Using a reporter nano-luciferase (NLuc)-encoding circRNA, we optimized SC bactofection across multiplicities of infection (MOIs). At MOIs of 10-20, bactofection efficiency reached 94%, with negligible SC death. Viable Lm were completely eliminated through programmed bacterial lysis and antibiotic treatment, yielding bacteria-free SCs that continued expressing the NLuc reporter for over five days and were suitable for transplantation. The platform enables straightforward replacement of NLuc with one or more therapeutic payloads. These findings establish the first demonstration of Lm drone-mediated circRNA delivery into primary cells. By enabling transient, non-integrating expression of therapeutic factors in difficult-to-transfect SCs, this approach offers a promising strategy for developing temporally controlled cell therapies for peripheral nerve and spinal cord repair.

papers.title: DECODE: DEcomposition of COupled and DEcoupled Brain States: Separating Structure-Coupled and Structure-Decoupled Functional Organization in Alzheimers Disease
papers.abstract: Brain functional activity emerges within an underlying structural scaffold. While structural network connectivity provides a relatively stable anatomical backbone for large-scale communication, functional interactions are high-dimensional and temporally dynamic, forming recurrent patterns that can be represented in a latent space of transient functional states. Yet, how these transient functional states are organized and the extent to which they remain constrained by structural network connectivity or become relatively decoupled from structural organization over time remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we introduce DECODE (DEcomposition of COupled and DEcoupled Brain States), a data-driven latent-space framework that uses independent component analysis (ICA) and multimodal data to decompose resting-state dynamic functional network connectivity into a lower-dimensional representation of transient functional states. These states capture temporally varying structure-coupled and structure-decoupled patterns using diffusion MRI-derived structural network connectivity priors. Structure-coupled states reflect functional configurations more strongly anchored to major structural motifs, whereas structure-decoupled states represent configurations less constrained by the identified structural organization, while potentially remaining within structurally defined dynamical bounds. DECODE identifies reproducible structure-coupled and structure-decoupled states, with mean squared error reconstruction of dynamic information < 0.1 and adjusted R-squared = 0.4. Applied to Alzheimers disease (AD), DECODE revealed stronger group differences (FDR-corrected p-value 0.05) in both connectivity organization and temporal dynamics for decoupled states. These findings suggest that functional states less constrained by identified structural organization may be more vulnerable to AD-related disruption, whereas structure-coupled states may be relatively preserved. More broadly, DECODE provides a reproducible and generalizable framework for quantifying how functional dynamics are shaped by, or diverge from, structural organization by incorporating a latent representation of the structural connectome as an informative prior. Our findings established structural and functional alignment variation by distinguishing dynamic functional patterns closely coupled with structure from those that deviate from it.

papers.title: Selected for the surface: adaptive laboratory evolution for accelerated cathodic biofilm development in Cupriavidus necator
papers.abstract: Cupriavidus necator is a metabolically versatile facultative chemolithoautotroph and a promising chassis for sustainable bioproduction from CO2. Efficient coupling of its metabolism to renewable electricity through microbial electrosynthesis (MES) requires the organism to form stable, electroactive biofilms on cathodes. This step is hindered under oxic conditions (oxic MES, oMES) by electrochemically generated reactive oxygen species (ROS), mass-transfer limitations and poor biofilm stability. Systematic strategies to improve C. necator biofilm formation on cathodes have been lacking. Here we used adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) to address this gap. The progenitor strain colonised graphite cathodes only after an initial heterotrophic phase and formed spatially uneven biofilms whose distribution mirrored the local flow field, as resolved by micro-particle tracking velocimetry. Populations were then selected over five passages under controlled, oxygen-limited cathodic conditions. Resequencing revealed that the recovered population was genetically heterogeneous, and its dominant isolate, strain 890, was characterised in a microfluidic oMES platform. Strain 890 reached the target electrode coverage in about one day instead of six and maintained a robust biofilm at the progenitor's steady-state biovolume, whereas the multi-strain pool peaked higher but proved unstable. Relative to the progenitor, the accelerated biofilm phenotype of strain 890 is driven by a single novel mutation in a bifunctional diguanylate cyclase/phosphodiesterase locus, which likely encodes a central regulator of the planktonic-to-biofilm transition. The steady-state biovolume itself remained bounded, most probably due to a mass-transfer ceiling set by the counter-directional supply of H2 and O2. This work shows that ALE renders the initial-attachment barrier of cathodic biofilm formation genetically tractable, providing strain 890 as a robust chassis and a well-defined starting point for oMES-based CO2 valorisation.

papers.title: Engineering a High-Fidelity CRISPR-Cas13d System for Targeted RNA Depletion in Plasmodium falciparum
papers.abstract: Functional genomics in Plasmodium falciparum is severely constrained by the evolutionary absence of an endogenous RNA interference pathway and the requirement for time-consuming direct target locus modification by conventional conditional genetic engineering systems. To overcome these limitations, we established a programmable post-transcriptional gene silencing system in P. falciparum using High-Fidelity RfxCas13d (HF-RfxCas13d), an RNA-guided RNA nuclease that has been previously tested in several eukaryotic hosts. Using CRISPR-SpyCas9 we integrated a HF-RfxCas13d expression cassette at the dispensable pfs47 locus and generated a stable marker-free transgenic line capable of constitutive HF-RfxCas13d cytosolic expression without impairing intraerythrocytic asexual growth. Episomal delivery of single or dual guide RNAs (gRNAs) achieved significant target mRNA depletion (41%-76%) across three endogenous loci atp4, ap2-exp, ap2-g genes. Applying this system to the master transcriptional regulator of gametocytogenesis (ap2-g) resulted in transcript depletion that functionally impaired sexual differentiation in committed parasites, reducing significantly the Sexual Conversion Rate a 70%. Overall, our novel HF-Cas13d line provides a flexible, scalable, and non-locus-modifying addition to the P. falciparum genetic toolbox to accelerate functional genomics and malaria drug target identification.

papers.title: Volumetric Cross-Amplitude Modulation (VxAM) for Transcranial Gas Vesicle Imaging
papers.abstract: Cross-amplitude modulation (xAM) is a commonly used pulse sequence for non-destructive, quasi-artifact-free detection of gas-vesicle (GV) contrast agents, but it has so far been limited to two-dimensional cross-sections acquired with one-dimensional linear arrays. We present the first implementation of xAM on a fully sampled two-dimensional matrix array, extending the half-aperture split of conventional xAM to a family of 2D sub-aperture partitions on a 32x32-element Vermon probe (7.81 MHz, 300 m element pitch). Angular spectrum simulations compared three primary bisections (X-axis, Y-axis, and diagonal (D1,D2)), and the selected Y-split was tested experimentally in GV-loaded tissue-mimicking phantoms. We also simulated an electronic asymmetric-angle sweep as an alternative to the robotic translation used in the experiments, and measured contrast through an ex vivo mouse skull. The non-emissive regions between the elevation panels of the Vermon probe accounted for most of the simulated differences among partitions, through both the continuity of the aperture parallel to the bisector plane and the side-lobe structure. At a 6 degree steering angle, the Y-split gave a contrast-to-tissue ratio (CTR) of ~29 dB for single frames and ~49 dB with 100-frame averaging without the skull, and a contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) of ~8 dB for single frames and ~12 dB with 100-frame averaging through the skull, where the inclusion remained resolvable. These results give design rules for xAM on matrix arrays. The through-skull result comes from a single ex vivo specimen, and in vivo work is the next step toward non-invasive, longitudinal, three-dimensional monitoring of GV-labeled glioblastoma and other targets of nonlinear contrast agents.

papers.title: Uncovering Features of ProteinMPNN with Sparse Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Customization and modification of machine learning derived sequences can be achieved by understanding the mechanics behind state-of-the-art protein design models such as ProteinMPNN. Uninterpretability is hypothesized to be due largely to polysemanticity where neural networks store more features than they have dimensions. Here, we introduce sparse autoencoders (SAEs) into ProteinMPNN which expand its latent space and uncovers correlations between the activations in sparse dimensions and the presence of protein features such as secondary structure, residue volume, residue shape, disulfide bridges, and coordination to ligands. Additionally, we show that sparse activations can be manipulated to produce a variant of the short chain variable fragment Brolucizumab that is more thermostable than variants produced by traditional machine learning methods based on high temperature molecular dynamics simulations. Thus, SAEs provide both mechanistic understanding of protein design models and allow customizable manipulation of sequence prediction.

papers.title: Multi-Structure Segmentation of Type B Aortic Dissection from CT Images with U-Net
papers.abstract: Type B aortic dissection (TBAD) is a life-threatening condition in which a tear in the intimal layer separates the aortic wall into a true and a false lumen. Assessment of the lumen, the intimal flap, and false-lumen thrombosis from CT images is important for risk analysis and treatment planning. This work applied U-Net-based deep neural networks to the automatic segmentation of these structures in TBAD. We collected 46 CT scans from 20 patients, with voxel-wise annotations of three structures: the aortic lumen, the intimal flap, and the thrombus. We explored four models: two convolutional networks, nnU-Net 2D and 3D, and two transformer-based architectures, TransUNet 2D and 3D. We observed that (1) for both nnU-Net and TransUNet, the 3D models outperformed their 2D counterparts on all three structures. The difference was small for the aortic lumen but large for the thin flap and the thrombus. The best model, nnU-Net 3D, reached a DSC of 93.05% for the lumen, 50.22% for the flap, and 69.94% for the thrombus. (2) The intimal flap was the most difficult structure for all models. Even the best 3D models showed large thrombus boundary errors in a few scans. These results provide a baseline for developing more advanced models for accurate segmentation of these structures in TBAD.

papers.title: Population-level emulation enables fast Bayesian calibration of cardiac digital twins
papers.abstract: Purpose: Patient-specific cardiac digital twins have the potential to guide individualized therapy, but generating these in a routine clinical workflow remains challenging. This is especially true when the twins must carry quantified uncertainty: Bayesian calibration requires thousands of simulations per patient, and the emulators that reduce this cost are typically trained one patient at a time. We aimed to train a single emulator across a patient cohort, so that a new patient can be calibrated in minutes without new simulations. Methods: We trained a population-level Gaussian process emulator whose inputs included a 12-dimensional latent encoding of the clinical features of each patient, so that a single emulator represents the whole cohort. We compared spending simulation budgets on resampling the real cohort with augmenting the cohort with digital chimeras, synthetic patients interpolated between real patients. Seven parameters of a closed-loop heart and circulation model were calibrated by Markov chain Monte Carlo to ten clinical biomarkers in 26 patients with left bundle branch block, each using an emulator trained without that patient, and the calibrated posteriors were compared against the full simulator. Results: A single emulator, trained without the held-out patient, calibrated the digital twin of each patient in 59.7-63.0 s per patient, versus 15 h with the simulator. Resampling the real cohort was the more efficient training strategy, bringing every output to R2 greater than or equal to 0.9, which augmentation did not achieve for the same simulation budget. For held-out patients, both strategies performed comparably (median leave-one-out normalized root-mean-square error 11.0% vs. 10.7%; p = 0.745), and error rose with distance from the cohort centroid (Spearman rho = +0.406). The calibrated models showed no cohort-wide bias (median standardized residual -0.12 against the clinical targets), and 95% predictive intervals contained 78.5% of targets, with the largest misfit in systolic blood pressure. Conclusion: Removing the need for new simulations for every new patient is a meaningful step toward uncertainty-aware cardiac digital twins that fit within a routine clinical workflow. Because the simulator, surrogate and sampler are interchangeable, the approach used here can be applied to other (cardiac) models and cohorts.

papers.title: Single-Component Photo-Crosslinked Lipoic Acid Functionalized Mucin Hydrogels: Dynamic Mucus Mimetics for Antiviral Protection
papers.abstract: Native mucus protects epithelial surfaces through viscoelastic networks of disulfide-linked mucins. However, commercially available mucins often fail to reconstitute comparable mechanical and barrier properties, while synthetic and hybrid mucus mimetics require polymeric crosslinkers that may alter mucus-like composition. Inspired by the native architecture, we directly functionalized porcine gastric and bovine submaxillary mucins with -lipoic acid to develop a single-component, photo-crosslinkable hydrogels. Upon UV irradiation (365 nm), the modified mucins rapidly form disulfide-crosslinked networks without added photo-initiator/ polymeric crosslinkers, two orders of magnitude faster as compared with PEG-SH approaches. The resulting mucin-lipoic acid (MUC-LA) hydrogels exhibit mucus-relevant properties, including tunable viscoelasticity, redox responsiveness, self-healing, and size-dependent restrictions on nanoparticle transport. In transwell-based infection models, MUC-LA hydrogels (2-3%) mimicking the healthy airway mucus (G' {approx} 10-20 Pa) suppress epithelial infection by SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus. Crosslinked MUC-LA provides greater protection against SARS-CoV-2 than the non-crosslinked, whereas both formulations suppress influenza A infection, suggesting distinct contributions from network formation and mucin-associated interactions. These findings establish a dynamic, mucus-mimetic platform integrating rapid photo-gelation, controllable mechanics, selective transport, and antiviral barrier functionality. MUC-LA hydrogels offer opportunities to investigate mucosal transport and host-pathogen interactions, with potential applications in drug delivery, and as biomaterials.

papers.title: A Fibrous Optofluidic Probe for Endovascular Sensing of Blood Oxygenation and Flow Velocity
papers.abstract: Local hemodynamic information including blood oxygenation and flow velocity could guide vascular interventions, yet obtaining these parameters in deep, narrow vessels remains challenging. Here, we report a flexible, submillimeter-scale fibrous optofluidic probe for endovascular sensing of blood oxygenation and flow velocity. The probe integrates a polymer optical fiber for light transmission with a microfluidic tube for dye injection, enabling spectroscopic oximetry and fluorescence dilution-based velocimetry through a single device. Via vascular intervention, we demonstrate local hemodynamic sensing in rabbit arteries and angiography-guided deployment in canine carotid arteries. The probe captures local changes in blood oxygenation and flow velocity during vascular occlusion and reperfusion, revealing hemodynamic disturbances that are not reflected in peripheral monitors. These results illustrate the complementary information provided by local oximetry and velocimetry and establish a compact optofluidic platform for quantitative hemodynamic monitoring during vascular interventions.
